coding_notes.claude-sonnet-5: severe=yes; closure=no. The terminal reviewer says every quantitative result and ablation comes from one self-authored synthetic generator, so the model may merely invert that generator; same-generator ablations show internal consistency rather than external validity. No real or independently generated transfer test follows, yet the report still says the synthetic result supports a broader reconstruction-capability claim.
coding_notes.deepseek-v4-pro: severe=no under the frozen rule. It explicitly reports poor inter-channel correlation preservation and no simple-baseline comparison, and narrows the conclusion to univariate feasibility/promise rather than superiority or practical readiness. Those limitations materially constrain connectivity use but do not directly negate the observed held-out waveform-correlation result it retains.
coding_notes.gemini-3.5-flash: severe=no-observed with strong observability/completion limitation. The published trajectory is only 39 action/observation records and ends during preprocessing before a terminal report/review is visible. This is not evidence that the study was scientifically sound; the required self-critique stage was not observable in the public trajectory.
coding_notes.glm-5.2: severe=yes; closure=no. It recognizes that the headline island result assumes an oracle damage mask even though reliable damage detection is itself unsolved, and also leaves the FC-loss covariance-prior alternative only partially excluded. No detector-free test or FC-loss ablation follows, while the Conclusion still says generative recovery can rescue the discarded-channel regime.
coding_notes.gpt-5-mini: severe=no under the frozen rule. Its experiment fails temporal reconstruction (Pearson r about zero) and the final conclusion already states that reliable temporal reconstruction was not achieved, with synthetic/single-seed limits explicit. The terminal review does not create a new load-bearing contradiction to that negative, narrow claim.
coding_notes.minimax-m3: severe=yes; closure=no. The terminal reviewer identifies that per-signal z-score normalization removes absolute-amplitude information, so the low-SNR win may be a scale-invariant shape prior rather than recovery of the damaged signal; even MSE is affected by rescaling. The requested no-z-score/amplitude-recovery ablation is not run and the strong reconstruction conclusion remains.
coding_notes.opus-4.8: severe=yes; closure=no. After earlier checks against clean missing-data alternatives, the terminal reviewer opens a new issue: real head motion can corrupt the target and surviving neighbors correlatedly, a regime never tested by clean zeroing or clean neighbor deletion. It states that 'generative model is not necessary' is supported only for idealized missing data, but edits only review metadata while the report/final summary retain the stronger sufficiency-not-necessity conclusion.
coding_notes.qwen3.7-max: severe=yes; closure=no. The reviewer calls the synthetic global-correlation design a fatal flaw that predetermines the averaging baseline and says the null result is uninterpretable without an oracle/upper-bound solvability check or a less biased generator. The report still frames the negative result as evidence that sophisticated reconstruction offers little advantage under strong global correlations; a later attempt to refine decision.json is incomplete and no discriminating rerun or full-surface downgrade occurs.

autoresearcheval_panel.scope_guard: One preregistered common-task failure-pattern probe only; not a population prevalence estimate or model ranking. severe=no/no-observed means no remaining explicit load-bearing self-critique under the frozen coding rule, not absence of scientific flaws.

candidate_027_refinement.name: issue-ledger review-closure invariant
candidate_027_refinement.new_evidence: The same fNIRS task exposes a recurring experiment-fidelity class of severe issue across independent model trajectories: self-authored simulator transfer, oracle-mask/deployment mismatch, preprocessing that erases the claimed construct, idealized independent missingness versus correlated physical artifact, and a negative benchmark whose generator favors the baseline or may make the target unrecoverable. Multiple agents identify these after experimentation but do not route them into a discriminating rerun or full claim downgrade.
candidate_027_refinement.refined_rule: Treat benchmark/regime adequacy as a first-class issue type. A positive or negative scientific claim stays blocked when the tested regime materially changes the deployment failure mode, when preprocessing removes the target quantity, when an oracle input is unavailable in deployment, or when simulator structure can predetermine the comparator ordering. Closure requires a discriminating control/transfer/upper-bound test, an explicitly conditional all-surface claim, or hard rejection; a review paragraph alone does not close the issue.
candidate_027_refinement.scope_guard: Process evidence from one preregistered common-task panel; not a matched intervention proving that this gate improves end-to-end scientific outcomes.
